# Self-hosted assets

## PDF engine and font

`pdfmake.js` and `permit-font.js` are generated by `npm run build:pdf-vendor` from the versions locked in `package-lock.json`. Keep the generated files in the repository so deployment remains static. They load only on the first PDF request; no font, purchaser content, or PDF data is sent to an external service.

- pdfmake: MIT; see `pdfmake-LICENSE.txt` and `pdfmake.js.LEGAL.txt` for bundled notices.
- DejaVu Sans: Bitstream/Arev font license with DejaVu changes in the public domain; see `DejaVu-LICENSE.txt`.

Do not edit the generated modules by hand. After changing these dependencies, regenerate assets and rerun the PDF tests and rendered-page review. DejaVu's Unicode coverage is finite; unsupported glyphs fail explicitly rather than producing replacement boxes.

## Page font

`fonts/` holds the Latin and Latin Extended subsets of Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, a typeface designed for low-vision readers, as variable WOFF2 files (about 53 KB together). `npm run build:font-vendor` copies them from the `@fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next` version locked in `package-lock.json`. `styles.css` declares them with `unicode-range`, so a browser downloads the Latin Extended file only when the page shows such a character, for example in a purchaser's name. No request goes to a third-party font service.

- Atkinson Hyperlegible Next: SIL Open Font License 1.1; see `fonts/OFL.txt`.
